title: New EPF Scheme, 2026 is in force
summary: The Employees' Provident Fund Scheme, 2026 (under the Code on Social Security, 2020) replaced the 1952 scheme. It was notified on 29 June 2026 and applies from 1 July 2026. Your UAN and balance do not change. The withdrawal and settlement rules on this site follow the new scheme.

title: Partial withdrawal: 3 categories, 12 months of membership
summary: The old 13 withdrawal reasons are merged into three: Essential needs (illness, education, marriage), Housing needs, and Special circumstances. A uniform 12 months of membership is needed. Education can be claimed up to 10 times and marriage up to 5 times. Under Special circumstances you no longer have to state a reason. Most claims need no documents.
source: EPFO CBT 238th meeting, 13 Oct 2025; EPF Scheme 2026

title: 25% of your PF must stay in the account
summary: For partial withdrawals, a minimum balance of 25% of contributions (your share, employer share and interest) stays in the account so it keeps earning interest. In practice you can take up to about 75%, now including the employer share. The 25% is released only on full settlement (retirement, 12 months of unemployment, permanent disability, moving abroad and similar events).

title: Lost your job? Full PF after 12 months, EPS after 36 months
summary: Premature final settlement of PF now needs 12 months of continuous unemployment (earlier 2 months). Withdrawal of the pension (EPS) part needs 36 months (earlier 2 months). While you wait, you can still take a partial withdrawal of up to the eligible 75%.
source: EPFO CBT 238th meeting, 13 Oct 2025; EPF Scheme 2026

title: When you can take 100% of your PF
summary: Full settlement is allowed on retirement after age 55, permanent and total disability, permanent migration abroad or employment overseas, retrenchment, voluntary retirement, and after 12 continuous months without covered employment.

title: EPFO must settle claims within 20 days
summary: The new scheme sets a 20-day deadline to settle a complete claim, and provides penal interest (12%) for delay without sufficient cause. Quote this when you escalate a delayed claim.

title: Auto-settlement up to ₹5 lakh
summary: Advance claims up to ₹5 lakh can be settled automatically, without an officer checking them, if your KYC is complete: Aadhaar linked and verified, PAN verified, bank account seeded and verified. Clean KYC is the single biggest reason claims go through fast.

title: Transfer PF without employer approval
summary: Since a circular of 15 Jan 2025, most online transfer claims (Form 13) skip employer attestation when your UAN is Aadhaar-verified and details match. From 25 Apr 2025 the destination PF office no longer has to process the transfer: once the source office approves, the money and your pension service move automatically.

title: Fix your name, DOB and other details yourself
summary: With an Aadhaar-verified UAN, you can self-correct common errors (name, date of birth, gender, nationality, parents' names, marital status, spouse name, dates of joining and leaving) online, without employer verification. If your UAN was issued before 1 Oct 2017 the employer may need to make the change. If Aadhaar is not linked, a physical Joint Declaration through the employer is still needed.

title: PF wage ceiling raised to ₹25,000
summary: The statutory wage ceiling went from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 a month from 17 Sep 2026, the first change since 2014. The employer's pension (EPS) share can now be up to ₹2,083 a month, which raises future EPS pensions. Existing EPF members earning up to ₹25,000 who were outside EPS are being brought into it.

title: EPF interest for FY 2025-26: 8.25%
summary: The CBT recommended 8.25% for FY 2025-26, unchanged from the previous two years. Interest is credited after the government notifies the rate, so the credit date varies.

title: PF withdrawal by UPI or ATM: announced, not yet live
summary: EPFO 3.0 plans withdrawals through UPI and ATM cards, and testing was reported complete in mid-2026. As of our last check there was no general public launch. Use only routes shown on the official EPFO portal or UMANG app, and ignore links or calls offering 'instant PF by UPI'.

title: TDS on PF before 5 years of service
summary: If you withdraw your PF balance before 5 years of continuous service (earlier jobs count if you transferred the balance) and the amount is more than ₹50,000, EPFO deducts TDS: 10% if PAN is linked, a much higher rate if not. Form 15G/15H can avoid TDS if your total income is below the taxable limit. After 5 years of continuous service the withdrawal is tax-free. This was Section 192A; under the Income-tax Act, 2025 it is Section 392(7) from 1 Apr 2026.

title: Your EPS pension: the 10-year line
summary: With less than 10 years of pensionable service you can take a withdrawal benefit (Form 10C) or keep a Scheme Certificate to carry the service forward. Under 6 months of service gives nothing. At 10 years or more, there is no lump sum: you get a monthly pension from 58 (reduced pension possible from 50). Pension = pensionable salary × pensionable service ÷ 70. Pensionable salary is capped at the wage ceiling.

title: NPS: up to 80% lump sum for non-government subscribers
summary: For All Citizen and Corporate NPS subscribers, normal exit now allows up to 80% as lump sum with at least 20% used to buy an annuity (earlier 60:40). Government sector subscribers stay at 60:40.

title: NPS exit by corpus size
summary: Non-government normal exit: corpus up to ₹8 lakh, take 100% (or withdraw it systematically). ₹8–12 lakh: up to ₹6 lakh as lump sum, the rest by systematic unit redemption over at least 6 years or as annuity (or use the 80:20 route). Above ₹12 lakh: up to 80% lump sum, at least 20% annuity.

title: Exit after 15 years, stay invested till 85
summary: Non-government subscribers can make a normal exit at 60 or after 15 years of subscription, whichever is earlier. Anyone can defer withdrawal or annuity purchase up to age 85 (earlier 75).

title: Leaving NPS early: 20% lump sum, 80% annuity
summary: Premature exit: if the corpus is ₹5 lakh or less you can take it all. Above ₹5 lakh, only 20% comes as lump sum and at least 80% must buy an annuity. The 5-year minimum before premature exit has been removed for non-government subscribers; it still applies to government subscribers.

title: NPS partial withdrawal: 4 times before 60
summary: After 3 years in NPS you can withdraw up to 25% of your own contributions (not the employer's, not the returns). Up to 4 times before 60 with a 4-year gap; after 60, once every 3 years. Purposes include children's education and marriage, buying or building a first house, medical treatment, and settling a loan taken against NPS. Skill development and starting a business were removed as purposes.

title: Loan against your NPS
summary: A regulated lender can now mark a lien on up to 25% of your own NPS contributions and lend against it, while the corpus stays invested.

title: NPS withdrawal tax: only 60% is tax-free
summary: At exit, a lump sum up to 60% of the corpus is tax-free. PFRDA now allows 80%, but tax law has not been changed to match, so the extra 20% is taxed at your slab. Annuity income is taxed every year at your slab. Partial withdrawals (up to 25% of own contributions) are tax-free. Budget 2026 made no NPS tax changes.

title: NPS tax deductions: old vs new regime
summary: New regime: only the employer's NPS contribution is deductible, up to 14% of basic + DA. Old regime: employer contribution up to 10% of basic + DA (non-government), your own contribution within the ₹1.5 lakh 80C limit (capped at 10% of salary), plus an extra ₹50,000 for your own contribution. Employer contributions to EPF, NPS and superannuation together above ₹7.5 lakh a year are taxable. Section numbers changed under the Income-tax Act, 2025; the benefits are the same.

title: Multiple Scheme Framework: up to 100% equity
summary: Non-government subscribers can hold schemes under the Multiple Scheme Framework, some of which allow up to 100% equity. The standard Active Choice equity cap for the common scheme is 75%.

title: EPS pension: early, deferred and the yearly life certificate
summary: You can start a reduced EPS pension from age 50: it is cut by 4% for every year you are short of 58. You can also defer it to 60 and get 4% more for each year deferred. Members with 20 or more years of service get 2 extra years of weightage at 58. The minimum EPS pension is ₹1,000 a month. Pensioners must submit a life certificate (Jeevan Pramaan, digital) once a year to keep the pension running.

title: Interest on large PF contributions is taxable
summary: Interest on your own PF contributions (including VPF) above ₹2.5 lakh a year is taxable as income. The limit is ₹5 lakh where the employer does not contribute. Your balance up to 31 March 2021 and its interest stay tax-free. The rule continues under the Income-tax Act, 2025.
source: Income-tax Act provisos to s.10(11), 10(12), carried into the 2025 Act

title: EDLI: up to ₹7 lakh life cover for your family
summary: If a PF member dies while in service, the family gets EDLI insurance of 35 times the average monthly PF wage plus half the average PF balance (that part capped at ₹1.75 lakh), with a minimum of ₹2.5 lakh and a maximum of ₹7 lakh. The higher ₹25,000 wage ceiling makes the maximum reachable for more people. Nominees claim it with Form 5IF, along with PF (Form 20) and family pension (Form 10D).

title: PF keeps earning interest until 58, even after you stop working
summary: Interest is credited to your PF account up to age 58, even if no contributions come in. After 58 the account becomes inoperative and stops earning interest, so claim it. Accounts with no transactions for 3 years face extra verification before withdrawal.

title: Open an NPS account with UPI in three clicks (NPS Tatkal)
summary: PFRDA has unveiled UPI-based NPS account opening that reuses your bank KYC, aimed at bringing 2–3 crore new subscribers in two years. NPS had about 2.3 crore subscribers in October 2026. Check availability in your bank or UPI app before relying on it.
